The '''2016–17 season''' was '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]'s''' 118th in existence and [[FC Barcelona|the club]]'s [[La Liga#Clubs|86th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. Barcelona was involved in four competitions after winning the [[Double (association football)|double]] of [[2015–16 La Liga|La Liga]] and the [[2015–16 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] in the [[2015–16 FC Barcelona season|previous season]]. This would be the final season under head coach [[Luis Enrique]] as he decided to let his contract expire.

Barcelona kicked off the season with en emphatic 5–0 aggregate victory over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the Supercopa de España, but the rest of the season was more mixed. The most memorable highlights were the historic [[FC Barcelona 6–1 Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|6–1]] comeback win against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the return leg of the Champions League round of 16, overturning the heavy 0–4 away defeat, and the 3–2 last-minute away league victory in ''El Clásico'' over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 23 April, courtesy of a [[Lionel Messi]] strike. However, these performances did not yield trophies in the aforementioned competitions, as Barça was shut down by [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the Champions League quarter-finals (0–3 away, 0–0 home) and lost the league title to Real Madrid by three points. The only consolation was a third consecutive Copa del Rey win on 27 May against [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].

The season was the first without [[Dani Alves]] since [[2007–08 FC Barcelona season|2007–08]], who departed to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], though he returned for a second spell in the [[2021–22 FC Barcelona season|2021–22]] season.

==Season overview==
===June===
On 1 June, the club announced that [[Sandro Ramírez]]'s contract would be rescinded.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/noticias/barca/robert-confirms-sandro-will-allowed-leave-barcelona-this-summer-5154811 |title=Robert confirms Sandro will be allowed to leave Barcelona. |work=Sport|location=Spain |date=24 May 2016 |access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref>

On 2 June, Barcelona announced that [[Dani Alves]] would be departing the club after eight seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/dani-alves-to-leave-fc-barcelona-this-summer |title=Dani Alves to leave Barcelona this summer. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 June 2016 |access-date=2 June 2016}}</ref>

On 3 June, Barcelona announced that [[Bundesliga|German]] club [[Borussia Dortmund]] have informed them of their desire to activate the buy-out clause for [[Marc Bartra]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/marc-bartra-to-join-borussia-dortmund |title=Bartra to join Borussia Dortmund. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 June 2016 |access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref>

On 5 June, the club announced that [[Denis Suárez]] will be forming part of the first team for this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/denis-suarez-two-years-of-development |title=Denis Suárez, two years of development. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=5 June 2016 |access-date=5 June 2016}}</ref>

===July===
On 1 July, Barcelona and [[Neymar]] negotiated a five-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |date=1 July 2016 |title=Neymar extends contract until 2021. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/neymar-contract-extension-2021-fcbarcelona/ |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=1 July 2016}}</ref>

On 4 July, the club completed the transfer of Denis Suárez.<ref>{{cite news |date=4 July 2016 |title=Denis Suárez returns to Barça. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/denis-suarez-joins-fcbarcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=4 July 2016}}</ref>

On 12 July, the club announced the transfers of 22-year-old [[France national football team|French international]] defender [[Samuel Umtiti]] from [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]]<ref>{{cite news |date=12 July 2016 |title=Umtiti second signing for Barcelona. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/samuel-umtiti-segon-fitxatge-del-fc-barcelona-2016/samuel-umtiti-second-signing-for-fc-barcelona-201617 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=12 July 2016}}</ref> and [[Lucas Digne]] from [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] for the next five seasons, respectively.<ref>{{cite news |date=12 July 2016 |title=Digne becomes Barcelona's latest signing. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/lucas-digne-becomes-fc-barcelona-s-latest-signing |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=12 July 2016}}</ref>

On 14 July, the two transfers were completed.<ref>{{cite news |date=14 July 2016 |title=Digne's officially a Barcelona player. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/lucas-digne-is-officially-an-fc-barcelona-player |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=14 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=14 July 2016 |title=Umtiti arrives in Barcelona. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/samuel-umtiti-arrives-in-barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=14 July 2016}}</ref>

On 19 July, Barcelona and [[Sergi Samper]] negotiated a three-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2019, including promotion to the first team.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 July 2016 |title=Samper extends contract to 2019. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/samper-extends-contract-to-2019 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref>

On 19 July, Barcelona and [[Munir El Haddadi]] also negotiated a three-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2019.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 July 2016 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/munir-renews-until-2019 |title=Munir renews until 2019. |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref>

On 19 July, Barcelona and [[Qatar Airways]] extended sponsorship agreement for one year more.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 July 2016 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-and-qatar-airways-extend-sponsorship-agreement |title=Barcelona and Qatar Airways extend sponsorship agreement. |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=19 July 2016}}</ref>

On 21 July, Barcelona and [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese international]] midfielder [[André Gomes]].<ref>{{cite news |date=21 July 2016 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/agreement-with-valencia-for-andre-gomes |title=Agreement with Valencia for André Gomes. |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> On 26 July, the transfer was completed.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 July 2016 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/andre-gomes-first-hours-as-an-fc-barcelona-player |title=André Gomes' first hours as a Barcelona player. |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=26 July 2016}}</ref>

During the press conference of Gomes' presentation, the club announced midfielder [[Javier Mascherano]]'s contract was extended until 30 June 2019.<ref>{{cite news |date=27 July 2016 |title=Mascherano extends contract until 2019. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/javier-mascherano-extends-contract-until-2019/ |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref>

On 30 July, Barcelona won their first pre-season match against [[2015–16 Scottish Premiership|Scottish champions]] [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] with a 1–3 score in [[Dublin]] as part of the [[2016 International Champions Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |date=30 July 2016 |title=Barça open the pre-season with a 3–1 victory over Celtic. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-open-the-pre-season-with-a-3-1-victory-over-celtic-fc |publisher=FC Barcelona}}</ref>

===August===
On 1 August, the club cancelled the contracts of [[Alex Song]] and [[Martín Montoya]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-and-alex-song-agree-to-terminate-contract |title=Barça and Song agree to terminate contract. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 August 2016 |access-date=1 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/agreement-to-cancel-martin-montoya-s-contract |title=Agreement to cancel Montoya's contract. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 August 2016 |access-date=1 August 2016}}</ref>

On 3 August, Barcelona defeated [[2015–16 Premier League|English Premier League champions]] [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] 4–2 in [[Stockholm]] with goals from Munir (2), [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[FC Barcelona B|Barcelona B]] player Rafa Mújica.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2016-2017/international-champions-cup/barcelona-leicester-city?tabType=report |title=Barça beat Leicester City. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 August 2016 |access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

On 6 August, Barcelona were soundly defeated by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 4–0 at [[Wembley Stadium]] in [[London]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2016-2017/international-champions-cup/liverpool-barcelona?tabType=report |title=Liverpool beat up on Barça (4–0). |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=6 August 2016 |access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

On 8 August, the club loaned [[Thomas Vermaelen]] to [[Serie A|Italian]] club [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] with an option to buy.<ref>{{cite news|title=Vermaelen loaned to Roma. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/thomas-vermaelen-loaned-to-as-roma |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 August 2016 |access-date=8 August 2016}}</ref>

On 10 August, the [[2016 Joan Gamper Trophy]] was played against Italian club [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], finishing 3–2 with a goal from Luis Suárez and two from [[Lionel Messi]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2016-2017/joan-gamper-trophy/round-3/barcelona-sampdoria?tabType=report |title=Barça keep the Gamper home. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=10 August 2016 |access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

On 14 August, Barcelona won the first official match in the [[2016 Supercopa de España]] against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] with a 0–2 away score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/sevilla-fc-v-fc-barcelona-half-way-there-0-2- |title=Sevilla v Barcelona: Half way there! (0–2). |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 August 2016 |access-date=14 August 2016}}</ref>

On 18 August, Barcelona beat Sevilla with 3–0 (5–0 aggregate) and won their 12th Supercopa de España.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-win-12th-spanish-super-cup |title=Barça win 12th Spanish Super Cup. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=18 August 2016 |access-date=18 August 2016}}</ref>

On 20 August, Barcelona defeated [[Real Betis]] 6–2 in their first Liga match, with a hat-trick from Luis Suárez, two goals from Messi and one from [[Arda Turan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-real-betis-back-with-a-bang-6-2- |title=Barcelona v Betis: Back with a bang (6–2). |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=20 August 2016 |access-date=20 August 2016}}</ref>

On 25 August, the club completed the transfer of 27-year-old goalkeeper [[Jasper Cillessen]] from [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] on a five-year contract,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/jasper-cillessen-joins-fc-barcelona |title=Cillessen joins Barcelona. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 August 2016 |access-date=25 August 2016}}</ref> with goalkeeper [[Claudio Bravo]] then joining [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] after two years with Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/08/25/claudio-bravo-signs-for-city/1472119073317 |title=Bravo signs for City. |publisher=ManCity.com |date=25 August 2016 |access-date=25 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825142732/http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/08/25/claudio-bravo-signs-for-city/1472119073317 |archive-date=25 August 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Several hours later, both teams were drawn into [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group C|Group C]] of the Champions League draw, alongside [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] and Celtic.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d81b9ebb1b5-0d9c9d16c91a-1000--uefa-champions-league-group-stage-draw/ |title=UEFA Champions League group stage draw |publisher=UEFA |date=25 August 2016 |access-date=25 August 2016}}</ref>

On 28 August, Barcelona defeated [[Athletic Bilbao]] 0–1 with a goal from [[Ivan Rakitić|Rakitić]] and [[Luis Enrique (footballer)|Luis Enrique]] wins his 100th match as Barça manager,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/athletic-club-v-fc-barcelona-three-huge-points-at-san-mames-0-1- |title=Athletic Club v FC Barcelona: Three huge points at San Mamés (0–1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=28 August 2016 |access-date=28 August 2016}}</ref> [[Ter Stegen]] made most goalkeeper passes in one single match in LaLiga.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/barcelona/2016/08/28/57c33a11e5fdeaa2688b45b2.html |title=Récord de pases en LaLiga para Ter Stegen |work=Marca|location=Spain|date=28 August 2016 |access-date=28 August 2016}}</ref>

On 30 August, the club completed the last transfer of [[Paco Alcácer]] from Valencia.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/paco-alcacer-signs-for-fc-barcelona |title=Paco Alcácer signs for FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=30 August 2016 |access-date=30 August 2016}}</ref>

===September===
On 10 September, in the match against Deportivo Alavés, Barcelona suffered a 1–2 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-alaves-newboys-stun-camp-nou-1-2- |title=FC Barcelona v Alavés: Newboys stun Camp Nou (1-2). |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=10 September 2016 |access-date=10 September 2016}}</ref>

On 13 September, Barcelona defeated Celtic 7–0 in the opening match of Group C in the Champions League. Messi notched his first hat-trick of the season, while Neymar provided four assists and a [[direct free kick|free-kick]] goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-open-champions-league-play-with-a-7-0-rout-of-celtic-fc |title=Barça open Champions League play with a 7–0 rout of Celtic. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=13 September 2016 |access-date=13 September 2016}}</ref>

On 17 September, Barcelona faced for the first time recently promoted [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] at the [[Estadio Municipal de Butarque]]. Barcelona won 1–5 with two goals from Messi and one each from Luis Suárez, Neymar and [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/five-star-fc-barcelona-too-good-for-leganes-1-5- |title=Barça get back to winning ways. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=17 September 2016 |access-date= 18 September 2016}}</ref>

On 21 September, Barcelona drew against Atlético Madrid 1–1; Ivan Rakitić gave Barça the lead before half-time, but Atlético battled back to draw level in the second half after Messi was substituted out due to injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-atletico-madrid-one-point-each-1-1- |title=FC Barcelona v Atlético Madrid: One point each (1–1). |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=21 September 2016 |access-date=13 September 2016}}</ref>

On 24 September, Barcelona won 0–5 over [[Sporting de Gijón]] through two goals from Neymar and one each from Suárez, Turan and Rafinha.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/sporting-gijon-v-fc-barcelona-barca-prove-a-handful-at-el-molinon-0-5-|title=Sporting Gijón v FC Barcelona: Barça prove a handful at El Molinón (0-5) {{!}} FC Barcelona|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=2016-09-25}}</ref>

On 28 September, Barcelona defeated Borussia Mönchengladbach 1–2 with goals from Turan and [[Gerard Piqué]], turning around a 1–0 first-half deficit to Barça top of Group C.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/second-half-heroics-lift-fc-barcelona-to-a-2-1-victory-over-borussia-monchengladbach |title=Second-half heroics lift FC Barcelona to a 2–1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach. |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=28 September 2016 |access-date=28 September 2016}}</ref>

===October===
On 2 October, Barcelona lost to [[Celta de Vigo]] 4–3; a second-half resurgence not enough for Luis Enrique's side as they finished on the wrong end of a seven-goal thriller away in [[Vigo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/battling-fc-barcelona-suffer-balaidos-blues-4-3- |title=Celta Vigo v FC Barcelona: Battling Barça suffer Balaídos blues (4-3) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 October 2016 |access-date=2 October 2016}}</ref>

On 15 October, Barcelona defeated [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] 4–0 with two goals from Rafinha and one each from Luis Suárez and Messi, the latter who returned from injury in the match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-deportivo-la-coruna-back-in-the-saddle-with-a-4-0-victory |title=FC Barcelona v Deportivo La Coruña: Back in the saddle with a 4–0 triumph |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=15 October 2016 |access-date=15 October 2016}}</ref>

On 19 October, Barcelona defeated [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] – led by former Barça manager [[Pep Guardiola]] – 4–0 at home on the strength of a Messi hat-trick.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-manchester-city-maestro-messi-shows-the-way-4-0- |title=Match Report: FC Barcelona v Manchester City: Maestro Messi shows the way (4–0) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 October 2016 |access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref>

On 22 October, Barcelona defeated Valencia 2–3 at Mestalla, Messi spot-kick in injury time secured three points out of an electrifying encounter.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/valencia-2-3-fc-barcelona-late-penalty-wins-nail-biting-thriller |title=Valencia 2-3 FC Barcelona: Late penalty wins nail-biting thriller |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 October 2016 |access-date=22 October 2016}}</ref>

On 29 October, Barcelona won against Granada 1–0 in the 1,500th game at Camp Nou, Barça found it tough to breakdown the stubborn visitors but Rafinha's strike was enough to claim the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-granada-persistence-pays-off-1-0- |title=FC Barcelona v Granada: Persistence pays off (1-0)
 |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 October 2016 |access-date=29 October 2016}}</ref>

===November===
On 1 November, Barcelona was defeated by Manchester City 3–1 at Manchester, Guardiola's team came from behind after Messi opened scoring.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/manchester-city-3-1-fc-barcelona-shaken-not-stirred |title=Manchester City 3-1 FC Barcelona: Shaken, not stirred |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 November 2016 |access-date=1 November 2016}}</ref>

On 6 November, Barcelona won 1–2 against Sevilla at the Sánchez Pizjuán; Messi canceled out Vitolo's opener late in the first half before setting up Luis Suárez for the winner in a frenetic game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/sevilla-v-fc-barcelona-messi-magic-inspires-comeback-win-1-2- |title=Sevilla v FC Barcelona: Magic Messi inspires comeback win (1-2) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=6 November 2016 |access-date=6 November 2016}}</ref>

On 16 November, the club announced [[Rakuten]] signed up as FC Barcelona's new main global partner; the Japanese company will appear on the front of the team's shirt and become the Global Innovation and Entertainment Partner for the next four seasons, starting 1 July 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/news/2016-2017/rakuten-sign-up-as-fc-barcelona-s-new-main-global-partner |title=Rakuten sign up as FC Barcelona's new main global partner |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=16 November 2016 |access-date=16 November 2016}}</ref>

On 19 November, Barça drew Málaga 0–0, a domineering performance was frustrated by 90 minutes of intense Andalusian defending.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-0-0-malaga-cf-deadlocked |title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Málaga CF: Deadlocked |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 November 2016 |access-date=19 November 2016}}</ref>

On 23 November, Barcelona won 2–0 against Celtic at [[Celtic Park]]; coupled with Man City's draw in Germany, they clinched a seeded berth in the round of sixteen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/celtic-fc-0-2-fc-barcelona-group-c-champions- |title=Celtic FC 0-2 FC Barcelona: Group C champions! |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 November 2016 |access-date=23 November 2016}}</ref> Also in this game Messi reached 100 goals in international competitions for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/leo-messi-s-100-goals-in-international-competition |title=Leo Messi's 100 goals in international competition |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 November 2016 |access-date=23 November 2016}}</ref>

On 27 November, Barcelona drew 1–1 with Real Sociedad at Anoeta, Messi's second-half leveller halted Barça's run of four straight league losses in San Sebastian.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/real-sociedad-v-fc-barcelona-anoeta-battle-ends-even-1-1- |title=Real Sociedad v FC Barcelona: Anoeta battle ends even (1-1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=28 November 2016 |access-date=28 November 2016}}</ref>

On 30 November, Barcelona drew [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] 1–1, a fine long range strike from debutant Aleña gave Barça a slight advantage going into the second leg.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/hercules-cf-v-fc-barcelona-holders-held-1-1- |title=Hércules CF v FC Barcelona: Holders held (1-1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=30 November 2016 |access-date=30 November 2016}}</ref>

===December===
[[File:2016-17 FC Barcelona at the Match of Champions.jpg|thumb|upright=1.3|2016–17 FC Barcelona at the Match of Champions]]

On 3 December, Barcelona drew 1–1 with Real Madrid, Luis Suárez' header being cancelled out by 90th minute Ramos equaliser.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-1-1-real-madrid-cruel-late-blow |title=FC Barcelona 1-1 Real Madrid: Cruel late blow|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=3 December 2016 |access-date=3 December 2016}}</ref>

On 6 December, Barcelona won 4–0 against Borussia Mönchengladbach, a game which saw a hat-trick from Arda Turan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-borussia-monchengladbach-group-stage-sealed-in-style-4-0- |title=FC Barcelona v Borussia Mönchengladbach: Group stage sealed in style (4-0)|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=6 December 2016 |access-date=6 December 2016}}</ref>

On 10 December, Barcelona won Osasuna 0–3, Luis Suárez breaks the deadlock in the second half, and two further goals from Leo Messi go on to claim all three points in Pamplona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/ca-osasuna-0-3-fc-barcelona-that-will-do-nicely- |title=CA Osasuna 0-3 FC Barcelona: That will do nicely!|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=10 December 2016 |access-date=10 December 2016}}</ref>

On 12 December, Barcelona were drawn against Paris Saint-Germain in the round of 16 of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0234-0e95e0cadb9c-eaaa62ace796-1000--champions-league-round-of-16-draw-bayern-v-arsenal-paris-v/ |title=Champions League round of 16 draw: Bayern v Arsenal, Paris v Barcelona |publisher=UEFA |date=12 December 2016 |access-date=12 December 2016}}</ref>

On 15 December, Barcelona and Suárez negotiated a five-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 December 2016 |title=Luis Suárez at FC Barcelona until 2021. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/luis-suarez-at-barca-until-2021 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=15 December 2016}}</ref>

On 18 December, Barcelona won 4–1 against Espanyol in the [[Derbi barceloní]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-rcd-espanyol-derby-delight-4-1- |title=FC Barcelona v RCD Espanyol: Derby delight! (4-1)|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=18 December 2016 |access-date=18 December 2016}}</ref>

On 21 December, Barcelona won 7–0 against Hércules; Paco Alcácer scored his first official goal and Arda Turan got a hat-trick as Barça cruised into the last 16 of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-hercules-through-in-style-7-0- |title=FC Barcelona v Hércules: Through in style (7-0)|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=21 December 2016 |access-date=21 December 2016}}</ref>

On 23 December, Barcelona was drawn against Athletic Club in the round of 16 of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-drawn-against-athletic-club-in-copa-del-rey-last-sixteen |title=FC Barcelona drawn against Athletic Club in Copa del Rey last sixteen |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 December 2016 |access-date=23 December 2016}}</ref>

===January===
On 8 January Barcelona drew 1–1 with Villarreal, with Messi scoring the equalizer in the 90th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/villarreal-v-fc-barcelona-messi-rescues-point-1-1- |title=Villarreal v FC Barcelona: Messi rescues point (1-1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 January 2017 |access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref>

On 11 January, Barcelona won 3–1 against Athletic Bilbao, goals from Suárez, Neymar and Messi secured an action-packed victory that kept alive the quest for a third consecutive Copa del Rey trophy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-fc-barcelona-3-1-athletic-club-4-3-on-aggregate-the-trident-strikes-again |title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 3-1 Athletic Club (4-3 on aggregate): The trident strikes again |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=11 January 2017 |access-date=11 January 2017}}</ref>

On 14 January, Barcelona won 5–0 against Las Palmas, a brace from Luis Suárez and one each for Leo Messi, Arda Turan and Aleix Vidal gave Barça a winning home start to the league in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-las-palmas-fabulous-five-5-0- |title=FC Barcelona v Las Palmas: Fabulous five (5-0) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 January 2017 |access-date=14 January 2017}}</ref>

On 19 January Barcelona won 0–1 against Real Sociedad, Neymar's 21st-minute penalty ended decade of disappointments in San Sebastián.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/real-sociedad-0-1-fc-barcelona-anoeta-conquered-at-last |title=[MATCH REPORT] Real Sociedad 0-1 FC Barcelona: Anoeta conquered at last |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 January 2017 |access-date=19 January 2017}}</ref>

On 22 January, Barcelona won 0–4 against Eibar, a first-half strike from Denis followed by a goal each from the trident in the second secured another three points to stay within reach of the top two.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/eibar-v-fc-barcelona-keeping-up-the-pressure-0-4- |title=Eibar v FC Barcelona: Keeping up the pressure (0-4) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 January 2017 |access-date=22 January 2017}}</ref>

On 26 January, Barcelona won 5–2 against Real Sociedad, a brace from Denis Suárez and further goals by Leo Messi, Luis Suárez and Arda Turan sent Barça into the final four of the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-real-sociedad-on-to-the-semis-5-2-6-2-agg.- |title=FC Barcelona v Real Sociedad: On to the semis! (5-2, 6-2 agg.) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 January 2017 |access-date=26 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202195607/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-real-sociedad-on-to-the-semis-5-2-6-2-agg.- |archive-date=2 February 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 29 January Barcelona drew 1–1 with Real Betis, an incident-packed game saw Suárez snatched a draw in the 90th minute after the Catalans had already seen at least one valid equaliser overruled.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-real-betis-1-1-fc-barcelona-suarez-salvages-late-point |title=[MATCH REPORT] Real Betis 1-1 FC Barcelona: Suárez salvages late point |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 January 2017 |access-date=29 January 2017}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Barcelona won 2–1 against Atlético Madrid, Suárez and Messi put them in command but Griezmann's second half header kept Atlético alive.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-atletico-madrid-1-2-fc-barcelona-magnificent-display-puts-barca-in-semi-final-driving-seat |title=[MATCH REPORT] Atlético Madrid 1-2 FC Barcelona: Magnificent display puts Barça in semi-final driving seat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 February 2017 |access-date=1 February 2017}}</ref>

On 4 February, Barcelona won 3–0 against Athletic Club Bilbao, Paco Alcácer, Leo Messi, and Aleix Vidal all found the net.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-dispatch-athletic-club-3-0-as-patience-pays-dividends-in-la-liga |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona beat Athletic Club, 3–0, as patience pays dividends in the league title chase |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=4 February 2017 |access-date=4 February 2017}}</ref>

On 7 February, Barcelona draw 1–1 against Atlético Madrid, Luis Suárez's tap-in just before half-time was enough to see the Catalans into a fourth consecutive Copa del Rey final despite late drama which saw the visitors equalise and a player sent off.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-atletico-madrid-barca-battle-through-to-the-final-1-1-3-2-aggregate- |title=FC Barcelona v Atlético Madrid: Barça battle through to the final! (1-1, 3-2 aggregate) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=7 February 2017 |access-date=7 February 2017}}</ref>

On 11 February, Barcelona won 6–0 against Alavés. Luis Suárez (2), Neymar Jr, Leo Messi and Ivan Rakitic were on target, plus one own goal; Aleix Vidal suffered a very serious ankle injury late in the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-alaves-0-6-fc-barcelona-blazing-victory-in-vitoria |title=[MATCH REPORT] Alavés 0-6 FC Barcelona: Blazing victory in Vitoria |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=11 February 2017 |access-date=11 February 2017}}</ref>

On 14 February, Barcelona lost 4–0 against Paris Saint-Germain in the first leg of the first knockout round of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-paris-saint-germain-4-0-fc-barcelona-a-mountain-left-to-climb |title=[MATCH REPORT] Paris Saint-Germain 4-0 FC Barcelona: A mountain left to climb |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 February 2017 |access-date=14 February 2017}}</ref>

On 19 February, Barcelona won 2–1 against Leganés, Leo Messi's 90th-minute penalty won the game at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-v-leganes-late-salvation-2-1- |title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 2-1 Leganés: Late salvation |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 February 2017 |access-date=19 February 2017}}</ref>

On 26 February, Barcelona won 2–1 against Atlético Madrid, Rafinha's opener was quickly cancelled out by Godín's header but Messi sealed three points in the closing stages.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-atletico-madrid-v-fc-barcelona-precious-late-win-at-the-calderon-1-2- |title=[MATCH REPORT] Atlético Madrid 1-2 FC Barcelona: Precious late win at the Calderón |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 February 2017 |access-date=26 February 2017}}</ref>

===March===
On 1 March, Barcelona won 6–1 against Sporting Gijón, with goals from Messi, Suárez, Alcácer, Neymar Jr, Rakitić and an own goal at the Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-fc-barcelona-6-1-sporting-gijon-sizzling-barca-keep-up-the-heat |title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 6-1 Sporting Gijón: Sizzling Barça keep up the heat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 March 2017 |access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref> During the press conference after the match, Luis Enrique announced his decision to leave at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/luis-enrique-to-leave-fc-barcelona-at-the-end-of-the-season |title=Luis Enrique to leave FC Barcelona at the end of the season |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=1 March 2017 |access-date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

On 4 March, Barcelona won 5–0 against Celta, with goals from Messi (2), Neymar, Rakitic and Umtiti.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-fc-barcelona-5-0-celta-football-that-dreams-are-made-of |title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 5-0 Celta: Football that dreams are made of |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=4 March 2017 |access-date=4 March 2017}}</ref>

On 8 March, Barça came back from a 4–0 deficit in the first leg. In the second leg, they were up 3–1, but by way of scoring three goals in the last seven minutes, they advanced. Marc-Andre Ter Stegen's saves coupled with Neymar's brace and Sergi Roberto's goal at the death clinched the 6–5 aggregate win in what was hailed as one of the greatest comebacks in Champions League history.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-6-1-psg-miracle-makers- |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona 6-1 PSG: Miracle makers! (6-5 aggregate) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 March 2017 |access-date=8 March 2017}}</ref>

On 9 March, Barcelona and Rakitic negotiated a four-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |date=9 March 2016 |title=Agreement to renew Ivan Rakitic's contract through to 2021 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/agreement-to-renew-ivan-rakitic-s-contract-through-to-2021 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=9 March 2016}}</ref>

On 12 March, Barcelona lost to Deportivo la Coruña 2–1, two goals from corners condemned Barça to defeat in Galicia, with Luis Suárez scoring in between.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-deportivo-la-coruna-2-1-fc-barcelona-back-down-to-earth |title=[MATCH REPORT] Deportivo la Coruña 2-1 FC Barcelona: Back down to earth |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=12 March 2017 |access-date=12 March 2017}}</ref>

On 17 March, Barcelona were drawn against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the quarter finals of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0237-0e968564abfb-f677030fe9d8-1000--quarter-final-draw-bayern-v-real-madrid-juve-v-barcelona/ |title=Quarter-final draw: Bayern v Real Madrid, Juve v Barcelona |publisher=UEFA |date=17 March 2017 |access-date=17 March 2016}}</ref>

On 19 March, Barcelona won 4–2 against Valencia, with goals from Suárez, André Gomes and a brace from Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-fc-barcelona-v-valencia-too-hot-to-handle-4-2- |title=[MATCH REPORT] FC Barcelona 4-2 Valencia: Too hot to handle |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 March 2017 |access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref>

===April===
Barcelona defeated Granada on 2 April 1–4 away, goals from Suárez, Alcácer, Rakitic and Neymar handed Barça another three points to keep in close proximity of the top.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-granada-1-4-fc-barcelona-keeping-up-the-pressure |title=MATCH REPORT: Granada 1-4 FC Barcelona: Keeping up the pressure |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2 April 2016 |access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref>

On 5 April, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 3–0, with a goal from Suárez and two from Messi in 8 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-sevilla-quickfire-treble-brings-the-points |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona 3-0 Sevilla: Quickfire treble brings the win |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=5 April 2016 |access-date=5 April 2016}}</ref>

On 8 April, Barcelona lost to Málaga 2–0, ten-man Barça missed out on the chance to return to the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-malaga-2-0-barca-costly-defeat |title=Málaga 2-0 Barça: Costly defeat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 April 2017 |access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref>

On 11 April, Barcelona lost to Juventus 3–0, Barça could not break through Juve's rock-solid defense.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-juventus-3-0-fc-barcelona-uefa-champions-league-quarterfinals-barca |title=Italian marble: Juventus 3–0 FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=11 April 2017 |access-date=11 April 2017}}</ref>

On 15 April, Barcelona beat Real Sociedad 3–2, Barça edged past La Real in a hard-fought duel thanked to two goals from Leo Messi and one from Paco Alcácer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-3-2-real-sociedad-back-to-winning-ways |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona 3-2 Real Sociedad: Back to winning ways |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=15 April 2017 |access-date=15 April 2017}}</ref>

On 19 April, Barcelona drew 0–0 with Juventus, Barça bade farewell to the Champions League after being unable to break down a resilient Juve backline.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-0-0-juventus-access-denied |title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Juventus: Access denied |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=19 April 2017 |access-date=19 April 2017}}</ref>

On 23 April, Barcelona beat Real Madrid 3–2, Barça grabbed a dramatic victory at the Santiago Bernabéu thanks to an injury-time strike from Leo Messi to move joint-top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/real-madrid-2-3-fc-barcelona-epic-win-reignites-title-race |title=Real Madrid 2-3 FC Barcelona: Epic late win reignites title race |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 April 2017 |access-date=23 April 2017}}</ref> The Argentine star scored his 500th official goal in blaugrana colours at the same time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/leo-messi-reaches-500-goals-for-fc-barcelona-real-madrid-clasico |title=Leo Messi reaches 500 goals for FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=23 April 2017 |access-date=23 April 2017}}</ref>

On 26 April, Barcelona beat Osasuna 7–1, braces for Gomes, Messi and Alcácer, and a first ever Barça goal for Mascherano,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/javier-mascherano-scores-his-first-goal-for-fc-barcelona |title=Javier Mascherano scores his first goal for FC Barcelona |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 April 2017 |access-date=26 April 2017}}</ref> earned the points.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-v-osasuna-seven-heaven-7-1- |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona v Osasuna: Seven heaven (7-1) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=26 April 2017 |access-date=26 April 2017}}</ref>

On 29 April, Barcelona beat Espanyol 3–0, all goals after half time, including a Suárez brace and one from Rakitic, to stay top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/rcd-espanyol-fc-barcelona-clutch-win-in-cornella-0-3-match-report |title=RCD Espanyol – FC Barcelona: Clutch win in Cornellà (0-3) |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 April 2017 |access-date=29 April 2017}}</ref>

===May===
On 6 May, Barcelona beat Villarreal 4–1, Messi, Suarez and Neymar all scored to keep the Liga title challenge alive, in the process surpassing a combined 100 goals for a third consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/-match-report-barca-4-1-villarreal-pressure-pumping-victory |title=[MATCH REPORT] Barça 4-1 Villarreal: Pressure pumping victory|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=6 May 2017 |access-date=6 May 2017}}</ref>

On 14 May, Barcelona beat Las Palmas 4–1, Neymar Jr scored three of the four goals that meant the championship race would now go to the last weekend.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-ud-las-palmas-1-4-fc-barcelona-big-win-keeps-the-heat-on |title=UD Las Palmas 1-4 FC Barcelona: Big win keeps the heat on|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=14 May 2017 |access-date=14 May 2017}}</ref>

On 21 May, Barcelona won Eibar 4–2, Luis Enrique's men rally back from two goals down to claim victory on the final day of the league campaign but it was not enough to earn the title.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-4-2-eibar-comeback-win-but-title-escapes-barca |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona 4-2 Eibar: Comeback win, but title escapes Barça|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=22 May 2017 |access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref>

On 27 May, Barcelona won Alavés 3–1, Barça become the first side since the 1950s to win the Copa del Rey three years in a row, on Luis Enrique's last game in charge.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/match-report-fc-barcelona-3-1-alaves-copa-kings- |title=MATCH REPORT: FC Barcelona 3-1 Alavés: Copa Kings!|publisher=FC Barcelona |date=27 May 2017 |access-date=27 May 2017}}</ref>

On 29 May, Barcelona and Ter Stegen negotiated a five-year contract extension lasting until 30 June 2022.<ref>{{cite news |date=29 May 2017 |title=FC Barcelona extends Ter Stegen contract until 2022. |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/fc-barcelona-extends-ter-stegen-contract-with-until-2022 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=29 May 2017}}</ref>

==Players==

===Squad information===
